forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Council Tax collection rate of 96.43% in 2025-2026, above national average
news_drafts.lead: Collection improved to 96.43% in 2025-2026 from 96.3% in 2024-2025, outperforming the all-England average of 95.62% and the unitary council average of 95.76%. The council credits this to service transformation including a new single system and cloud migration.

findings.headline: LCTRS claimant numbers rise by 52 total and 181 working-age between June 2025 and June 2026
findings.detail: Total scheme recipients grew from 17,332 to 17,384, with working-age claimants increasing from 9,857 to 10,038. This rising demand for support is driving the cost increase and indicates growing economic stress among the resident population.
findings.matters: Rising dependence on support schemes signals economic conditions and household financial stress; growing claimant numbers increase the council's financial exposure if support rates are not adjusted and revenue continues to fall.
findings.quote: As of June 2025, the total number of people in receipt of LCTRS was 17,332 with 9,857 being of working age. As of June 2026, the total number of people in receipt of LCTRS is 17,384 with 10,038 being of working age.

findings.headline: Incoming Council Tax legislation from April 2027 expected to make collection more challenging
findings.detail: Major legislative changes take effect from April 2027, including delayed recovery cycles, expanded support for residents unable to pay, and a shift from 10 to 12 monthly payment instalments. The paper explicitly states these changes "will make collection more challenging for all authorities". Full details await the laying of legislation.
findings.matters: Changes to collection mechanics and support entitlements directly affect revenue timing and realisable income; this signals a sector-wide revenue risk ahead; the council flagged it as justification for maintaining current support levels.
findings.quote: Major changes to Council Tax legislation including delayed recovery cycles, greater support for those who are unable to pay Council Tax, and a move from 10 to 12 monthly payers are expected to be introduced from April 2027 which will make collection more challenging for all authorities.

findings.headline: Council Tax collection rate of 96.43% in 2025-2026, above national average
findings.detail: Collection improved to 96.43% in 2025-2026 from 96.3% in 2024-2025, outperforming the all-England average of 95.62% and the unitary council average of 95.76%. The council credits this to service transformation including a new single system and cloud migration.
findings.matters: Collection rates are a key metric of billing authority effectiveness and directly impact revenue realisation; peer councils compare performance; lenders assess cash-collection risk.
findings.quote: The Council Tax collection rate for WWNC for 2025-2026 is 96.43% which is an improvement on the collection rates for 2024-2025 of 96.3%. This compares well to an all-England national average of 95.62% and a national average for unitary councils of 95.76%

findings.headline: Council Tax Reduction Scheme cost rises to £21.6m for 2026-2027, up from £20.4m in 2025-2026
findings.detail: The scheme supporting working-age claimants cost £21.6m in 2026-2027, an increase of £1.2m (5.9%) from the previous year. This cost is reflected in foregone Council Tax revenue rather than funded separately. The council proposes keeping the scheme unchanged for 2027-2028 and anticipates this can be contained within existing budgets.
findings.matters: Rising cost of support schemes directly reduces effective Council Tax revenues; understanding the trajectory is essential for medium-term financial planning, particularly given incoming legislative changes.
findings.quote: The estimated cost of the scheme for 2026-2027 is £21.6m. This compares to £20.4m for 2025-2026.

findings.paper_title: WNC-Cabinet P4 GF and HRA capital monitoring FINAL
findings.headline: Temporary accommodation acquisitions pipeline budget of £10m removed from capital programme following review identifying insufficient service need.
findings.detail: A £10m pipeline budget for temporary accommodation acquisitions has been removed from the capital programme. Following a review, the service have confirmed this was no longer required because the existing approved budget for Provision of Relocatable Temporary Accommodation is sufficient for service needs. If requirements change in future, new budget requests will be reassessed through the governance process.
findings.matters: This shows the council adapting capital plans when prior assumptions change. It indicates a prior overestimation of accommodation need but demonstrates good governance and flexibility in capital planning.
findings.quote: The £10m pipeline budget for temporary accommodation acquisitions has been removed. Following a review, the service have confirmed that this was no longer required with the current budget for Provision of Relocatable Temporary Accommodation already in the approved programme being sufficient for service needs.
